- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 7–14 days.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% for next 7–14 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% to offset momentum.  
- Model frequently overcorrects after mean-reversion periods; if 3–5 consecutive days show price retracing toward 50-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate true price if sentiment is mixed or trending downward; add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment shows weak bullish or neutral bias.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model often misjudges turning points; adjust forecast to align with sentiment swing midpoint.
